long_biography.plain_text:
A national science competition recognized Bouton's high-school research in biology. He later studied neuroscience at Amherst and molecular neurobiology at Johns Hopkins. In the laboratory he built early tools for organizing gene-expression data, establishing the bridge between life science and computing that shaped his career.

At Pfizer, Bouton led integrative data mining and created an internal knowledge platform before turning to entrepreneurship. Entagen applied linked-data methods to pharmaceutical information and was sold to Thomson Reuters. His next venture, Vyasa, used deep learning to connect biomedical text, images and structured records. Following its acquisition, he brought that platform into Certara, where he directs technology strategy for AI-enabled biosimulation and medicine development.

A national science competition recognized Bouton's high-school research in biology. He later studied neuroscience at Amherst and molecular neurobiology at Johns Hopkins. In the laboratory he built early tools for organizing gene-expression data, establishing the bridge between life science and computing that shaped his career.

At Pfizer, Bouton led integrative data mining and created an internal knowledge platform before turning to entrepreneurship. Entagen applied linked-data methods to pharmaceutical information and was sold to Thomson Reuters. His next venture, Vyasa, used deep learning to connect biomedical text, images and structured records. Following its acquisition, he brought that platform into Certara, where he directs technology strategy for AI-enabled biosimulation and medicine development.
